newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba says develops cheap, chip-based smart card.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba says develops cheap, chip-based smart card.

text.p: Toshiba Corp said on Wednesday it had developed integrated circuit (IC) cards with special chips that are cheaper than existing versions and offer protection against forgery.
Toshiba said in a statement it would start shipping out samples in April and begin mass production in June. The cards will be marketed globally, it said.

They have a variety of uses, including as pre-paid telephone cards and discount cards, on which buyers accumulate credits towards new goods. Illegal copying of such cards is a growing problem in Japan.

The new cards, the CZ 3000 series, are priced at 100-200 yen (88 cents to $1.77) compared with rival products costing around 500-1,000 yen ($4.43 to $8.85) Toshiba said. The new cards have micro-controller chips.
These afford greater protection against forgery than regular IC cards. Toshiba said it planned to sell 12 million IC cards in the 1997/98 business year.
Hitachi Maxell Ltd introduced an IC card on Wednesday priced at 150 yen ($1.32). The cards, however, are not equipped with chips.
